title: podman stop: network teardown fails with "netavark: setns: IO error: Invalid argument" on kernel 6.12.0-211.7.3.el10_2; stale socket leaves published port bound but black-holed
body:
### Issue Description

`podman stop` (or systemd/quadlet stop) consistently fails during container network teardown on
kernel 6.12.0-211.7.3.el10_2.x86_64, with journal errors:

    Error: cleaning up container <id>: removing container <id> network: netavark: setns: IO error: Invalid argument (os error 22)
    unit: Control process exited, code=exited, status=125/n/a

Beyond the failed teardown, a stale socket survives on the container's published host port
(owned by conmon), so every TCP connect to that port times out afterwards. Every *fresh*
container created after such a failure has its published port black-holed the same way,
even though the iptables DNAT / nftables jump rules are all present and correct.
A host reboot clears both symptoms until the next failing teardown.

Same machine, same packages, kernel 6.12.0-211.49.1.el10_2.x86_64: zero failures across
dozens of start/stop cycles. Only difference between failing and clean runs is the kernel.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. AlmaLinux 10.2 host (bare-metal or VM), podman 5.8.2 / crun 1.27 / netavark 1.17.2, systemd 257, kernel 6.12.0-211.7.3.el10_2.x86_64
2. podman network create mynet (or systemctl start of any quadlet container unit with a published TCP port)
3. podman stop <container>   -> journal shows the EINVAL netavark/setns error above, exit status 125
4. systemctl/podman start the container again; curl its published port from localhost -> connect times out
5. podman exec/ss: socket still LISTEN on the published port, fd owned by conmon; any other new container's published port behaves identically

### Describe the results you received

- stop always fails at teardown with "netavark: setns: IO error: Invalid argument (os error 22)" (100% repro on the .7.3 kernel)
- published host port remains LISTEN (socket owner conmon fd5) but all connects to it time out
- subsequently created containers have their published ports dead in the same way despite valid DNAT rules
- firewalld ruleset verified correct (accept rules present) - firewall ruled out
- only cleared by a host reboot; recurs after further stops

### Describe the results you expected

stop succeeds (network teardown completes), unit reaches inactive cleanly, and the published port
serves the restarted (and any new) container on the same kernel that hosts containers without issue
(6.12.0-211.49.1.el10_2.x86_64 - dozens of stop/start cycles clean).

### podman info output

```yaml
      crun version 1.27

  os: linux

    Using metacopy: "true"

```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Privileged

### Upstream Latest Release

No

### Additional environment details

AlmaLinux 10.2, kernels:
  failing: 6.12.0-211.7.3.el10_2.x86_64 (ships in the OVH Alma 10.2 cloud image)
  clean:   6.12.0-211.49.1.el10_2.x86_64 (dnf install of the current el10_2 kernel)
systemd 257-23.el10_2.2.alma.1, SELinux enforcing, iptables frontend, default netavark network setup.
Repro box: pristine libvirt VM (fresh Alma 10.2), stock busybox httpd container, no custom CNI/firewall -
same signature also occurred on the original bare-metal host (Rocky 9, podman 5.9.4).

### Additional information

- Frequency: 100% of stops fail on .7.3 (journal shows every single teardown error); dozens of stop/start cycles clean on 49.1 on the same box/packages
- Workaround found: boot pin to 6.12.0-211.49.1.el10_2.x86_64 (fresh netavark network after upgrade clears leftover state)
- Since only the kernel changes between failing and clean runs, the EINVAL from setns() at teardown time (and the leftover socket state) may be kernel-side - feel free to point it to the right project/kernel bug tracker
- Reported against AlmaLinux 10.2 packages (podman 5.8.2 / crun 1.27 / netavark 1.17.2); not retried against upstream yet.

comments.body:
We have no time to debug distribution specific issues. You need to report this through the distro bug trackers as kernel regression if it clearly fails with the newer kernel.

We only support the lasted version upstream, the latest netavark should also have code to better cleanup when such error happen.
